posts.html: At the Democrat-organized watch party, Councilmember Bryce Goldstein expressed excitement for early progressive City Council leads, but told ChicoSol that in previous City Council races, early votes have skewed progressive before becoming a tighter race.
“I’m very confident I’m going to get reelected,” says Councilmember Tom van Overbeek.
Cheers erupted at the Democrat-organized watch party as the Associated Press called CA-1 in favor of Mike McGuire, the Democrat running to represent Chico in the House of Representatives.

Republicans at Park Side feel discouraged by the national turnout, but hold out hope for local elections. Mayor Kasey Reynolds says “it’s still early” and is looking forward to the next updates.
Half an hour after polls closed in Chico, all three progressive candidates showed early leads against their opponents. Full results will not be available for a while.

As the polling booth doors closed at 8 p.m. at the Silver Dollar Fairgrounds, poll workers packed up tables and took down their American flag. Manager Bertha Leyva has been working Election Day for 23 years. “We didn’t have long, long lines, but it was steady and it was good,” Leyva said. Another worker said that some of the Chico State students experiencing hour-long lines pivoted to the fairgrounds location. Around 8 p.m. at Chico State, the line still stretched around the building.

At a Democrat-organized watch party at B Street Public House, the energy vibrates as attendees watch Democrats win race after race across the nation. Progressive City Council candidate Shelby Hebert hopes this energy stays alive in California. “I feel hopeful for the first time in a while,” Hebert said as James Talarico’s victory in the Texas senatorial race was announced overhead.
While polls close at 8 p.m., results from Butte County are not expected right away.
Even on Election Day, Chico City Council will meet at 6 p.m. in the council chambers. Mayor Kasey Reynolds and councilmembers Addison Winslow and Tom van Overbeek are vying to hold their seats.
Voters have been waiting over an hour at Bell Memorial Union polling center, as voting line snakes around the building. While polls close at 8 p.m., voters in line by then will still be able to vote.
Voting is open until 8 p.m. For poll and ballot drop off locations, visit https://chicosol.org/2026/10/17/as-the-general-election-approaches-heres-what-you-need-to-know/
